content:
This month, Google released the all-new Pixel 11 series. Compared to last year's Pixel 10 series, the phone itself hasn't changed much, but there are some delightful improvements in the user experience. One of them is a new camera processing option that gives you finer control over the final look of your photos.

Hopefully, Apple does something similar before the iPhone 18 Pro arrives.

The Pixel 11 introduced a new camera feature called "Camera Looks." It's somewhat similar to the iPhone's "Photographic Styles," allowing you to adjust how the camera processes images before you take a shot. Because the adjustments happen before capture, it's more than just a standard filter.

Like Apple, Google offers several preset looks, and goes a step further by letting you fine-tune each one individually. There are also some brand-new looks that fit modern smartphone photography trends: Editorial, Velvet, Classic, Digi, Black Tie, and Minimal.

These looks intentionally move away from the heavily processed feel of typical smartphone photos, trying to recapture the flavor of old-school photography. True to its name, Digi focuses on delivering that limited dynamic range, high contrast, and grainy noise feel—just like those compact point-and-shoot cameras from the 2010s.

On the other hand, Minimal is an all-out low-processing look, where most HDR processing won't kick in, resulting in photos that more closely match what the phone's sensor actually captured. You can check out some sample photos over at 9to5Google.

Sure, using ProRAW on iPhone can lower the processing level, but that kind of defeats the purpose of shooting with a smartphone.

Wrap-up

If Apple wants to build the best camera that fits in your pocket, it needs to accept that not every user has the same needs. "Photographic Styles" was a good start, but Apple should take it a step further. Photography is fundamentally a form of self-expression, so giving users more choice over the degree of processing is an important next step. Apple should take a page from Google and add a Minimal style to iPhone.

What are your thoughts on the iPhone's current photography performance? Do you love Apple's latest "Photographic Styles," or do you feel it still falls short? Drop your thoughts in the comments.
